title: Causal Chain: Does Better Error Recovery Drive the Performance Gap Between Model Generations?

original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain: Does Better Error Recovery Drive the Performance Gap Between Model Generations?

**Problem:** Newer model generations (1.7 to 9.8 steps over 18 months) dramatically outperform older ones. This improvement may be driven by better error recovery rather than better initial attack choices — newer models may be better at recognizing when they are stuck and trying alternative approaches.

**Direction:** Analyze attack transcripts (from publicly available evaluations or generated in this study) by categorizing each step as: (A) first-attempt success, (B) failed, recovered correctly, (C) failed, stuck in loop, (D) failed, abandoned. Compare the distribution of A/B/C/D across 2-3 model generations (representing different capability levels). Test whether the improvement from older to newer models is concentrated in category B (error recovery) vs. A (first-attempt quality).

**Why it matters:** If newer models primarily improve by better error recovery, this implies that the architectural mechanism driving capability growth is feedback processing rather than domain knowledge. This predicts that capability gains will continue as reasoning improves and focuses attention on error-recovery training as a lever.

**Relevant context:** AISI: performance rose from 1.7 to 9.8 steps across 7 model generations. AISI identified NTLM relay bottleneck — potentially an error recovery failure. Context relay paper (NDSS 2026) proposed relay specifically for error recovery in long-running agents. AWS multi-agent architecture used specialized recovery sub-agent.
